newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close edge higher, blue chips lead.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close edge higher, blue chips lead.

text.p: Institutional buying in blue chips sent Seoul stocks to a higher close on Wednesday but concerns over the Hanbo Group's financial crisis kept overall sentiment bearish, brokers said.
The composite index closed 0.71 points higher at 663.56, after fluctuating widely between 654.95 and 672.90.
Brokers attributed the blue-chip rebound to the finance ministry's announcement on Tuesday of a plan to allow domestic investment firms to expand issues of beneficiary certificates.
Despite the index rise, decliners far outpaced advancers by 533 to 265, while 104 stocks remained unchanged.

The finance ministry said on Tuesday domestic investment firms would be allowed to issue up to $1-$1.2 billion worth of beneficiary certificates for foreign investors this year, up from $900 million in 1996.
"The finance ministry's plan and bargain hunting boosted buying in blue chips as investors believed blue chips would benefit most from the move," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities.
Samsung Electronics rose 1,600 won at 47,100, Korea Electric Power Corp gained 500 won to 27,400 and Korea Mobile Telecom added 15,000 won to 525,000.

The Hanbo Group has been in a financial crisis after its flagship unit Hanbo Steel Co defaulted on debt repayments last week. Hanbo Steel applied for court receivership on Tuesday along with its unlisted affiliate Hanbo Corp.
State prosecutors have launched investigation into loans to the Hanbo Group while the ruling and opposition parties agreed to a parliamentary probe into the scandal.
Brokers said the market was expected to rebound technically on Thursday, with an exception of bank shares that are expected to remain weak due to concerns about the impact from the Hanbo crisis.
"Banks will continue to face selling as investors are concerned about the impact on their earnings from the Hanbo crisis," said a Ssangyong Investment and Securities broker.

Seyang Shipping Co announced it was considering seeking court receivership or looking for a buyer due to financial trouble caused by Hanbo's debt default. It said financial institutions were avoiding deals with it because its largest shareholder is a brother-in-law of the Hanbo Group chairman.
The Korea Stock Exchange suspended trading in Seyang shares until Thursday.
